claims.text: Non-equiatomic HEAs are chemically disordered, compositionally complex, multi-element alloy systems.
Specialized interatomic potentials can be developed and calibrated to capture magnetic exchange interactions in non-equiatomic HEAs.
Specialized interatomic potentials can accurately capture magnetoelastic coupling in non-equiatomic HEAs.
Atomistic simulations using calibrated machine-learning or interatomic potentials can be applied to multicomponent HEAs.
The proposed approach is applicable to thin films or nanoparticle arrays near ambient to slightly elevated temperatures and under moderate magnetic fields.
Local magnetic exchange interactions and magnetoelastic coupling within the disordered lattice mediate the magnetic and magnetocaloric response.
Calibrated computational potentials can capture subtle magnetic transitions in these HEAs.
Simulations can map how compositional variations alter magnetic ordering.
The proposed potentials can predict composition-dependent shifts in magnetic transition temperatures.
The proposed potentials can predict composition-dependent magnetic entropy changes and magnetocaloric responses.
Detailed computational mapping will enable targeted tuning of the magnetocaloric effect through alloy composition.
The method will provide enhanced control over magnetic transition temperatures.
The method will improve magnetocaloric-effect magnitude or efficiency.
The exact sizes of the transition-temperature shifts and magnetocaloric improvements remain to be determined empirically.
HEAs modeled or synthesized without specialized potential calibration have less optimized and less predictable magnetocaloric behavior.
The method's effectiveness is limited to low-dimensional settings and moderate magnetic fields, with applicability to bulk materials or extreme conditions not guaranteed.
Quantitative predictions require experimental validation because their accuracy is uncertain.
Predictions from conventional and magnetically sensitive potentials can be compared against measurements on synthesized HEAs.
Magnetic transition temperature, isothermal entropy change, and strain-dependent magnetic response are proposed measurement variables.

The hypothesis is falsified if the new potentials do not provide a statistically significant improvement over conventional potentials in matching measured magnetic-transition and magnetocaloric properties.
